title: Run a scheduled, hashed official capture (Wed / Thu / Fri / kickoff)
why: The whole availability feature depends on being able to replay what was known before kickoff. Today there are two time points this season and no Wednesday or Thursday.

options.label: A
options.text: Collect nfl.com pages only (injuries, inactives article, schedule, scores, transactions, game centres). Four captures a week, sha256 per capture, drift alarm on row counts and required fields.
options.risk: Low - official domain, no terms question
options.tradeoff: Cheapest and safest, but leaves the depth question (Q06/Q07) unanswered.

options.label: B
options.text: Option A plus the 32 official club sites for depth charts and transactions.
options.risk: Medium - 32 parsers, one of which (the Texans) publishes an image
options.tradeoff: Closes the depth gap if the pages are parseable; high maintenance.

options.label: C
options.text: Option A plus a licensed data feed that carries depth, snaps and prices under a read licence.
options.risk: Medium - the price-data policy (SG-B) must be decided first
options.tradeoff: Fastest route to a full feature set; costs money and imposes terms.

recommended: A now, and do not start B or C until the sample from A has been read.

title: Decide the price-data policy before any backtest is published
why: No official page publishes a spread, total or moneyline. Every residual, CLV and ROI number in this repository is therefore undefined until a source and its terms are chosen.

options.label: A
options.text: Publish no price at all. Ship the model's fair line as a probability with its inputs and no market comparison.
options.tradeoff: Honest and immediate, but the brief's 'residual against the market' and CLV leaderboard cannot exist.

options.label: B
options.text: Ingest one licensed odds source, terms read and recorded, with open and close captured on a schedule.
options.risk: Medium - single-vendor dependence and a retention obligation
options.tradeoff: Unblocks residuals and CLV; every derived number inherits one vendor's definition of 'close'.

options.label: C
options.text: Ingest several sources and publish a vig-free consensus with the operator margin decomposed out.
options.risk: Medium - consensus construction must be pre-registered
options.tradeoff: Best separation of origination alpha from vig; slowest to stand up.

dependency: Blocks Q10 and Q16, and every leaderboard column that uses a market price.
recommended: A as the default today, with B or C chosen by the owner before any CLV claim.

title: Resolve the depth-order source before building the deficiency feature
why: The brief asks for 2nd/3rd/4th-string replacements. nfl.com publishes no depth chart (404) and no snap counts were found, so the feature currently has no input.

options.label: A
options.text: Per-club official depth pages, verified club by club, with a parser that records shared and empty slots faithfully.
options.risk: Medium - the Texans publish an image; jersey numbers must be stripped
options.tradeoff: Direct answer if all 32 cooperate; dead ends if some publish images.

options.label: B
options.text: Derive depth from snap counts using the official gamebook, once one has actually been retrieved and parsed.
options.risk: Medium - availability lag, and snaps measure the past
options.tradeoff: Measurable starter/backup split; cannot name a replacement before kickoff.

options.label: C
options.text: Build nothing until one route is verified for all 32 clubs.
options.tradeoff: Avoids fabricating a starter the club never named; leaves the feature absent.

recommended: C is the safe default; B is the better bet if a gamebook can be retrieved.

title: Transcribe the full live injury report into the repository
why: This session read the whole live page but only transcribed 8 of 28 clubs. The inactive-coverage finding (Q01) rests on 46 inactives; it should rest on all of them.

options.label: A
options.text: Transcribe all 28 clubs for Week 10 and recompute the join.
options.tradeoff: Triples the sample for one week; still one week.

options.label: B
options.text: Option A plus an automated fetch-and-parse step so future weeks need no transcription.
options.risk: Medium - needs the drift alarm from SG-A
options.tradeoff: The only route to a multi-season sample.

recommended: B, but only inside the SG-A collector.

title: Ingest the official reserve list and the six transaction categories
why: The reserve list exists and is dated (25 moves in November 2026), and it explains two of the three Out players who were missing from the inactive list - including the Malik Willis case the brief names. Nothing in this repository captures it, so 'not listed' still reads as 'available'.

options.label: A
options.text: Capture the reserve list alone, daily, hashed, and join it to the weekly injury and inactive captures. One page, one parser.
options.tradeoff: Closes the highest-value half of the gap immediately; leaves trades and signings out.

options.label: B
options.text: Capture all six categories (Trades, Signings, Reserve List, Waivers, Terminations, Other), and stamp every depth and availability row with the last roster event affecting it.
options.tradeoff: Makes roster turnover a first-class dated event, which the brief asks for; six parsers instead of one.

recommended: A this week, B as soon as the collector exists.

title: Complete the venue register to 14 of 14
why: Thirteen venues are captured from official pages; the Thursday game is missing because the inactives article covers Sunday games only.

options.label: A
options.text: Read the Commanders-Giants game centre and record its Location and Stadium fields.
options.tradeoff: Completes Week 10; does not generalise.

options.label: B
options.text: Make the venue a required field of the fixture capture, so every future fixture is captured with one.
options.tradeoff: Prevents the gap from recurring.

recommended: Both - A is one read, B is a drift-alarm field.

title: Add a freshness guard and re-read the Steelers-Bengals result
why: Both /schedules and /scores rendered that fixture as LIVE in the first quarter on 2026-11-16. Publishing a score from that state would be an inference.

options.label: A
options.text: Refuse to publish any score whose state is not Final, and record the fixture as blank plus flagged.
options.tradeoff: Correct, and leaves a hole until the page settles.

options.label: B
options.text: Option A plus a re-read job that clears the flag once the page reports Final, recording both the fetch time and the page state.
options.tradeoff: Self-healing, and leaves an audit trail of when the result became known.

title: One canonical count, computed at build time, never typed into prose
why: Three sessions published 254, 279 and 347 rows for the same page, and a fourth published 326. Counts written by hand go stale the moment a sibling merges.

options.label: A
options.text: Pin one capture file, compute every count from it, and fail the build if a page contains a count that is not produced by the parser.
options.tradeoff: Settles the discrepancy; requires touching pages that already type a number.

options.label: B
options.text: Option A plus a single shared register page that every namespace links to instead of repeating the number.
options.tradeoff: Removes the duplication that created the divergence.

dependency: The integration session, because it changes shared outputs.
recommended: A now, B at the next integration.

title: Consolidate the duplicated nfl-* namespaces into one canonical set
why: Thirty namespaces each publish their own questions, suggestions and review pages. Contradictory numbers are inevitable and are already present.

options.label: A
options.text: Freeze new namespaces and mark one canonical namespace per domain.
options.tradeoff: Stops the bleeding without deleting anyone's work.

options.label: B
options.text: Merge the canonical namespaces and keep the rest as archived research records, linked but not navigated.
options.tradeoff: A site a reviewer can actually use; needs an integration session.

recommended: A immediately, B at the next integration.

title: Capture roof, surface and weather per venue from published sources
why: Totals and passing props misprice when a dome is assumed outdoors or a windy open stadium is assumed calm. The official pages read this session publish neither.

options.label: A
options.text: Record the stadium and city from the Game Center for every fixture, and mark roof and surface blank until a source is found.
options.tradeoff: Honest, and builds the venue spine the overlay would hang on.

options.label: B
options.text: Option A plus an NWS grid capture per venue and an official roof/surface field where the league publishes one.
options.risk: Medium - mixes two domains and two timestamps
options.tradeoff: Enables the overlay; needs the timestamp discipline of SG-A.

recommended: A now; B only if the roof designation is actually published somewhere.

title: Put a control baseline on every leaderboard run
why: Without a random-pick and a favourites-only column, a good week is indistinguishable from a good model.

options.label: A
options.text: Publish random and favourites-only baselines beside every strategy, with the same n and the same proper score.
options.tradeoff: Needs a favourites definition; with no official price, 'favourite' must be defined from the model, not the market.

dependency: A defined benchmark (see SG-B option A).

title: Pre-register each strategy: rule text, window and gates, committed first
why: The commit hash is the registration. Without it, any leaderboard result can be accused - correctly - of being chosen after the fact.

options.label: A
options.text: A registration file per strategy: frozen rule text, sample window, gates, and the commit hash, created before the window opens.
options.tradeoff: Requires discipline; no cost otherwise.

options.label: B
options.text: Option A plus a gate that refuses to rank any strategy whose registration commit predates its first graded result.
options.tradeoff: Makes the rule enforceable rather than aspirational.

title: Split train, validation and final holdout by season
why: Out-of-sample testing is the only thing that separates a model from a curve fit.

options.label: A
options.text: Fix the split by season, publish which seasons are in which fold, and forbid touching the final holdout until the model is frozen.
options.tradeoff: Costs sample size in the short run.

dependency: A results corpus (SG-G plus the past-season archive).

title: Keep parlays and prop combos behind a joint-evidence gate
why: Multiplying marginal probabilities is invalid under dependence. Until a joint probability is validated on official results, a combination must not be ranked.

options.label: A
options.text: Rank singles only, and publish the combination gate as unmet.
options.tradeoff: Removes a whole product category until the evidence exists.

options.label: B
options.text: Estimate a dependence structure on official results and publish the joint probability with its uncertainty before ranking anything.
options.risk: High - dependence estimates need a large sample
options.tradeoff: The only route to ranking combinations honestly.

dependency: Q10, Q18 and a multi-season results corpus.

title: Publish n beside every correlation and every rate
why: A correlation without its n is not a number. The designation rates on this site are published with n = 26 and n = 4 precisely so they cannot be mistaken for settled facts.

options.label: A
options.text: Make n a required column on every correlation and rate table, and fail the build when it is missing.
options.tradeoff: None.
